original_question: For every real number epsilon > 0, if m is a sufficiently large even integer and A is a set of distinct reduced residue classes modulo m with |A| > (1/2 + epsilon) phi(m), must the triple sumset A + A + A contain every odd residue class modulo m?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in Section 1 (the introduction), i.e. Sárközy’s Problem 66 on triple sumsets of dense subsets of reduced residue classes modulo an even integer m.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the main mathematical content of the paper’s target statement: the quantifier over every epsilon > 0, the requirement that m be a sufficiently large even integer, the density threshold |A| > (1/2 + epsilon)phi(m), the fact that A is drawn from reduced residue classes modulo m, and the conclusion that the triple sumset should cover all odd residue classes modulo m. It is also correctly focused on the residue-class conjecture rather than the neighboring prime-number theorem.
missing_details: The ambient object should be stated explicitly: A is a subset of the unit group (Z/mZ)^* of reduced residue classes modulo m.
The triple sumset should be defined explicitly as 3A = A + A + A = {a1 + a2 + a3 mod m : a1,a2,a3 in A}.
The phrase 'for all sufficiently large m' should be unpacked as: for every epsilon > 0 there exists M(epsilon) such that the statement holds for every even integer m >= M(epsilon).
The modulus should be stated as a positive even integer.
The target set should be defined explicitly: 'every odd residue class modulo m' means every class x in Z/mZ with x ≡ 1 (mod 2).
The word 'distinct' is unnecessary once A is specified to be a set of residue classes.
refined_question:
For every real epsilon > 0, does there exist M(epsilon) such that, for every even integer m >= M(epsilon), every subset A ⊆ (Z/mZ)^* with |A| > (1/2 + epsilon)phi(m) satisfies
3A := {a1 + a2 + a3 mod m : a1,a2,a3 ∈ A} ⊇ {x ∈ Z/mZ : x ≡ 1 mod 2}?
justification: The draft is already very close to Conjecture 1.1: it has the correct density threshold, the correct parity restriction on m, the correct source set of reduced residue classes, and the correct 3-fold additive conclusion. The main refinements needed to make it fully stand-alone and paper-faithful are formal rather than conceptual: the paper works in residue-class notation, so A should be placed in (Z/mZ)^*, the sumset should be defined in Z/mZ, and 'sufficiently large' should be written with the quantifier order M = M(epsilon). The nearby Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 are part of the same introductory framing around this conjecture, but your draft is targeting the conjectural local residue-class statement itself, not the prime-number theorem proved later in the paper.
